Normals stay simple, without gags. Today's move-data clock (93 ticks, plank hitbox 20-35, IASA 47). Replaces Greatsword Swing (reference 'swing', the old clip on his body). Owner rule from the Joust (2026-10-21): show the first take before any revision. Second keys (2026-10-21 evening): the first keys turned the plank 180 degrees in three ticks while the chest turned 45 and were solved one at a time, so the left hand flipped round the handle and the take spent its 45 minutes fighting it (v1 brief in artifacts/sir-bonk-normals-20261021/bonk-sir-g2-barn-door.v1.json). Causes: the grip held the hands 23 cm apart (fixed in the pack: unity_rigpack.py grip --hand-gap 0.12) and the keys held the hands 27-34 cm from the chest below chest height with the elbows near 90 degrees. Now the arms reach out at chest height and the clip returns to the idle by tick 52 (v2 brief in artifacts/sir-bonk-normals-20261021). Fourth keys (2026-10-22): owner on the third keys: 'still not right... both hands try to be together on the handle, when in fact they could be side by side, as long as they're both approximately on the handle'. The exact grip.json lock winged the elbows (the left elbow up to 11 cm over the shoulder, the forearms crossing his face at tick 21). The keys' arms were re-solved with the toolkit's loose hold and elbows kept down (two_hand_grip(..., hold='loose', elbows=True); tmp/bonk-normals/g2-arms/resolve_keys.py), body and plank as keyed; the owner: 'looks better and probably good enough to accept'. Approved keys: artifacts/sir-bonk-normals-20261021/g2-keys-v4-loose.json (v3 brief in artifacts/sir-bonk-normals-20261021).

description:
Sir Bonk's ground 2, the Barn Door: his all-round normal, one big two-handed horizontal slice across his front, like a barn door swinging shut. The owner wants it two-handed and horizontal. It replaces his old Greatsword Swing (reference 'swing', played on his body).

Who he is. Sir Bonk is a huge, good-hearted, slightly dumb brute who read Don Quixote once and knighted himself (images 1 and 2). He has a blue mop-bucket helm with a broom crest, a cream tabard with his painted crown, pot-lid pauldrons and a cape, and he carries a plank greatsword. He is proud and determined. The owner wants his normals clean: no gags, the energy comes from his body.

His idle, where this move starts and ends (measured in the character frame): his feet are wide and square to the front. The plank rests back over his right shoulder: the right hand in front of the right chest (about 0.45 m above the hips), the blade rising behind him to his right at about 38 degrees, its tip about 1.15 m behind his hips and 0.9 m above the hilt. The left fist sits on his left hip.

How the game plays it. Ticks 0-93 at 60 Hz (1.55 s), played once; the game stretches the whole clip over the move, so author exactly these ticks. The game crossfades into the clip from his idle or his run over 0.05 s. The plank itself is the hitbox, from tick 20 to tick 35: whoever it sweeps through gets hit, so from tick 20 the plank must be sweeping across his front at chest height. From tick 47 the player can act again: the wind-up, the swing, the follow-through and the return to the shoulder must all read by tick 47. After that the clip only shows if the player waits. Tick 0 is his idle pose exactly, and ticks 52-93 are his idle pose exactly (`b.exit_pose`); the game then crossfades back to his idle.

The reference (image 3: ten key frames of the video, seen from his front three-quarter right, the camera of `front-three-quarter-right`; each frame's tick is in the brief's review beats). It sets the poses and the body mechanics, not the timing: the video takes about 4 s and holds every pose. Its white swoosh and flying cape are video artifacts. The video stops the swing pointing forward; ours carries on to his left (below).

The beats:
- Ticks 0-3: he leaves the idle. Its plank hand is folded back about 137 degrees off the forearm (hidden behind the plank); straighten that wrist by tick 4. The check skips ticks 0-3 for it.
- Ticks 3-8, the grip (video beat 2): the left hand leaves his hip and closes on the handle just below the right hand; the plank comes up nearly vertical in front of his right shoulder. Both hands stay on the handle from tick 5 to tick 43. The hold is loose (the brief's `two_hands_hold`): the left fist only has to sit on the handle beside the right hand, 8-16 cm below it, free to turn about it and slide along it (`two_hand_grip(..., hold='loose', elbows=True)`, `carry(..., hold='loose', elbows=True, both_ways=True)`).
- Ticks 8-13, the cock (video beat 3): a batter's stance, deep like the video's: both knees bent, the hips down about 8-12 cm. His chest turns 60-75 degrees to his right, the hips 30-40 degrees, the plank cocked high over his right shoulder with the tip back and up, both hands by the right shoulder. The left foot steps out about 45 cm forward and to his left, his weight back on the right leg.
- Ticks 13-16, the load (video beat 4): the deepest coil. The plank tips a little further back behind his head, the hips sink to about 10-14 cm below the idle, both knees bent, the left foot plants.
- Ticks 16-20, the swing (video beat 5): the hips whip round toward the front first, the chest follows a tick or two later. The plank drops to chest height and trails flat behind and out to his right, the hands leading it, held out from his body.
- Ticks 20-24, through (video beat 6): fast. The plank sweeps flat across his front at chest height; at tick 21 it points straight ahead of him.
- The arms reach out, elbows down. Through the whole swing (ticks 16-30) both arms reach out in front of his chest at chest height, the hands 50-75 cm from his chest, and both elbows hang below the shoulders and the hands, never winged up: the approved keys hold them 16-29 cm below the shoulders. Two attempts went wrong here. Take 2 folded the hands 27-34 cm from the chest, below chest height ('both his hands do weird shit'). The third keys locked the left hand onto one exact grip, which left the arms a single way to reach it: the elbows winged up and the forearms crossed in front of his face. The owner: 'both hands try to be together on the handle, when in fact they could be side by side, as long as they're both approximately on the handle'.
- The body turns the swing. From the load to the finish the chest turns about 130-150 degrees (from 60-75 to his right to 60-75 to his left) and the hips about 90; the arms and plank ride with the chest as one piece, so the plank's direction relative to the chest changes far less than its direction in the world (at most about 70 degrees from tick 15 to tick 27). That is what a big two-handed swing looks like, and it is what keeps both hands on the handle: the first keys turned the plank 180 degrees in three ticks while the chest turned 45, and the left hand had to flip round the handle.
- Ticks 24-30, the finish: the plank's weight carries the swing on, still flat, 45-70 degrees past straight ahead to his left, his chest turned to his left, the right heel up and the right foot pivoting on its ball, with a small overshoot.
- Ticks 30-38: a moving hold in the follow-through: the chest keeps turning a few degrees, the head settles, the plank drifts lower; nothing parks.
- Ticks 38-44, up (video beats 8 and 9): the hips lead him upright, the left foot draws back toward its idle place, and both hands lift the plank diagonally up to vertical in front of his right shoulder.
- Ticks 44-47, the shoulder (video beat 10): the plank tips back onto his right shoulder and the left fist returns to his hip. By tick 47 he stands in his hero stance.
- Ticks 47-52: straight into his idle pose, no separate settle (the game blends into the idle anyway; the owner does not care about this part). The plank wrist bends back into the idle's fold over ticks 44-52 (the check skips ticks 44-93 for it). Ticks 52-93 hold the idle pose exactly.

The right toes stay where they are: the heel may lift and the foot may turn on its ball, but it does not slide. The left foot steps out and back. A flat swing reads well from the match camera straight behind him: the plank crosses the whole screen, out to his right on the swing and out to his left on the finish. The plank stays clear of his bucket, crest, pauldrons, cape and legs, and its tip never goes into the floor (the floor is at up = -1.025 m in the character frame; with a flat foot the toe joint ToeBase sits about 0.05 m above it). The fighter does not move; the hips may shift.

The approved keys (`keys/result.json`) already hold the plank loosely with both elbows down: keep them. Between the two-handed keys use `carry(clip, keys, hold='loose', elbows=True, both_ways=True)` (guide, Contacts): it carries the plank in the chest's frame, keeps the left fist on the handle and the elbows down, and solves each stretch from both ends, so the arms arrive on each key's own solution (on these keys: 2-33 degrees from each key; the largest is the three-tick load-to-swing into tick 18, a speed, not a flip). Then give the motion its timing and flow. The guide's Flow section applies: stagger the arrivals (hips, then chest, then arms, then head) and key every hold as a moving hold. Fast motion belongs to the swing and the sweep (ticks 15-27). Do not animate the cape joints (Cape_L/C/R1..4): a spring drives them in the game, so leave them at their rest rotation. No props other than the plank. Keep each hand in line with its forearm (wrists under 45 degrees) outside the exempt ticks.
